title: Ribbit King
fan_note: A fan game after Bandai's Ribbit King (GameCube, 2003), made for a friend who loved it. Not affiliated with Bandai; every frog, course and picture here is new.
no_webgl: Ribbit King draws its courses with WebGL 2, which this browser does not offer. Try a recent Chrome, Firefox, Safari or Edge.

help_intro: Frolf is golf played with frogs. Each frog sits on a catapult; whack it with the mallet and the frog flies. Fewest strokes into the lotus wins, and the best frog on the card is crowned the Ribbit King.
help_rows: The swing

Aim with A and D (or the arrows), set the mallet's power with W and S, and change the loft with Q. The dotted arc shows where a perfect hit at that power first lands. Press Space: the needle starts round the dial. Press Space again to whack. In the gold is a perfect hit: full power, dead straight, a little extra, and a firework from the bell. Elsewhere on the red bar is weaker, and early hooks left, late slices right. Off the bar is a whiff.
In the air
You fly your frog. W A S D steer it, relative to the camera. Drag the view with the mouse to look around.
Three routes

Every hole is a par 5 or more with three ways to the lotus: out left, out right, and down the middle. The left and right routes cross on a high terrace in the middle of the hole; the middle one goes under it through a tunnel. Cliffs, rivers and waterfalls sit between them.
Survey the hole

Press V (or the Survey button) to rise over the hole and plan. W A S D move the view, the wheel or + and − zoom, and dragging turns it. The pin on the ground shows how far it is from your frog, how far on to the lotus, and how much higher or lower it sits. Your aiming arc stays drawn, so you can see where this shot lands. V or Space comes back down. Surveying moves only your own camera: online, nobody else's view changes.
Lily pads and webs
Lily pads throw you back up. Spider webs are strung across pits in the ground, from medium to extra large: land on one and it stretches down and flings you up, and a bigger web flings harder.
Giant blue mushrooms
They work like pinball bumpers: touch one and it bounces you away. The small red mushrooms are explosive and blast you up and away.
Power-ups
Extra jumps (Space in the air, carry three) and wings (glide: A D bank, W dive, S climb). Many sit out in the rough, off the fairways.
Bubbles
Floating bubbles are worth points, more for bigger ones and the risky ones. Points are counted apart from your strokes.
Flies
Each fly you catch is one small extra hop when you next land. Ten flies make the tongue ready: press E with another frog in reach to knock it flying.
Water
Frogs swim. Land in a river or pond and there is no penalty: a lily pad comes up under you and you play from there. Lava and out of bounds still cost a stroke.
Creatures

In the swamp, snails crawl across the fairways and block bounces, and whirlpools spin you round and throw you somewhere new. In the desert, antlions wait at the bottom of sandy pits: land near one and it grabs you, and your turn ends there.
Turns
Everyone tees off in order; after that, the frog farthest from the lotus plays next, as in golf. A hole is given up at five over par. The frog in first place wears a small crown.
Online

Choose Play, then Host online: the setup screen shows a room code. Others choose Play online on the title screen and type it. Empty seats (click a seat's button until it says Open seat) wait for players; each joiner picks their own frog, and the host picks the course and starts. On your turn you play from your own browser; on everyone else's you watch it live. If a player leaves, the CPU takes their frog.
